title: Severe IME candidate window misalignment when typing CJK characters on Windows @C:\Users\PC5080\.gemini\tmp\822e8215b009f46a641a99493e982cd82aecee13f183db24d50a086dbced0857\images\clipboard-1770708344776.png

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue reports a clear, reproducible UI rendering bug where typing CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) characters on Windows causes severe IME candidate window misalignment. The report includes version, OS, environment details, and visual screenshots.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Localized UI fix across 3 input components (InputPrompt.tsx, TextInput.tsx, BaseSettingsDialog.tsx). The fix replaces cpIndexToOffset(...) with getCachedStringWidth(cpSlice(...)) for terminalCursorPosition calculations.

summary.problem: IME candidate window misaligns when typing CJK characters in CLI input fields on Windows.
summary.root_cause: terminalCursorPosition passed to Ink's <Text> component is calculated using cpIndexToOffset (UTF-16 code unit offset) rather than visual string width (getCachedStringWidth). Single-code-unit CJK characters in the BMP have a visual width of 2, leading to underestimated cursor column positions in terminal coordinates.
summary.context: Ink uses terminalCursorPosition to emit ANSI cursor position sequences that Windows Terminal and IME popups use to anchor candidate selection windows.

steps: In packages/cli/src/ui/components/InputPrompt.tsx, update terminalCursorPosition calculation from cpIndexToOffset(lineText, cursorVisualColAbsolute) to getCachedStringWidth(cpSlice(lineText, 0, cursorVisualColAbsolute)).

In packages/cli/src/ui/components/shared/TextInput.tsx, update terminalCursorPosition calculation from cpIndexToOffset(lineText, cursorVisualColAbsolute) to getCachedStringWidth(cpSlice(lineText, 0, cursorVisualColAbsolute)).

In packages/cli/src/ui/components/shared/BaseSettingsDialog.tsx, update terminalCursorPosition calculation from cpIndexToOffset(editBuffer, editCursorPos) to getCachedStringWidth(cpSlice(editBuffer, 0, editCursorPos)).

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: terminalCursorPosition correctly reflects the visual width of CJK characters (2 columns per character) so the terminal cursor and IME candidate window align with the typing position.
verification_steps: Add a unit test in InputPrompt.test.tsx with CJK characters to assert terminalCursorPosition equals visual string width (4 for 2 CJK characters) instead of code unit count (2).
Run vitest on InputPrompt.test.tsx and TextInput.test.tsx to verify all cursor positioning tests pass.
